Our partner is looking for a Staff Site Reliability Engineer based in Ireland. This is a high-impact reliability leadership role within a fully remote engineering organization operating globally. The role combines hands-on engineering with organization-wide influence, covering observability, incident response, operational readiness, and resilience. Introduce and champion error budgets as a practical framework for balancing reliability investments with product and feature delivery. Establish and maintain the reliability metrics used by engineering leadership to evaluate progress and identify areas requiring investment. Strengthen the complete incident management lifecycle, including detection, response, communication, escalation, postmortems, and follow-up actions. Improve alert quality, anomaly detection, escalation processes, and shared operational tooling in collaboration with infrastructure teams. Lead reliability assessments for high-risk changes and new services, covering production readiness, capacity, failure modes, rollback strategies, and operational risks. Introduce deliberate failure testing, game days, and chaos exercises to identify weaknesses and validate safe operational limits before incidents occur. Work directly with engineering teams on complex reliability challenges through focused engagements, leaving behind stronger practices and clear ownership. Develop lightweight, repeatable operational standards covering production readiness, on-call practices, runbooks, change safety, and service operability. Partner with architects and technical leads to ensure reliability and failure tolerance are incorporated into system design rather than addressed after deployment. Promote effective use of AI for incident investigation, telemetry analysis, postmortem development, runbook creation, observability, and reliability tooling. Contribute production fixes and improvements directly through code and infrastructure changes rather than limiting the role to recommendations and reviews. Strong coaching and mentoring skills, with evidence of developing engineers into effective reliability owners. Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to clearly communicate incidents, risks, technical trade-offs, and reliability priorities to both engineers and executives. Practical experience using AI tools for incident investigation, telemetry analysis, runbook and postmortem development, and engineering tooling. Understanding of how operational data, alerts, dashboards, and runbooks should be structured to support safe AI-assisted diagnosis and operations. Pragmatic approach to reliability, with the ability to balance operational risk, engineering investment, delivery speed, and business priorities. Experience in fraud detection, identity, payments, or other real-time and adversarial environments is an asset. Experience with multi-region architectures, cell-based architectures, or failure-isolation strategies is a plus. Experience operating Elasticsearch, Redis, DynamoDB, or Kafka at scale and understanding their failure modes is beneficial. Familiarity with FinOps and cloud infrastructure cost-versus-reliability trade-offs is an advantage. Must be authorized to work from the hiring location; visa sponsorship is not provided. Basic Job Information Job Title : Utility-Scale BESS LTSA Service Director Department : Energy Storage Service Center Report To : Head of Energy Storage Service Work Location : Europe ( Remote ) Vacancy : 1 Job Attribute : Core management role, dedicated to utility-scale energy storage, responsible for contract performance, customer operation and full-cycle project management 2. Job Overview This role serves as the dedicated person-in-charge for LTSA (Long-Term Service Agreement) of the company’s utility-scale BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) business. You will fully oversee the commercial negotiation, clause implementation, contract performance, on-site operation and maintenance, risk control, customer relationship management and team management for all utility-scale BESS LTSA projects. Focusing on the full lifecycle services of grid-side, power supply-side and industrial & commercial large-scale energy storage power stations, you will take charge of core work including equipment maintenance, fault disposal, spare parts management and performance optimization. You need to ensure full compliance and KPI achievement of all ongoing LTSA projects, continuously improve customer satisfaction and project profitability, build a standardized and systematic LTSA service operation system, and support the long-term operation and secondary commercial value appreciation of the company’s existing energy storage projects. 3. Core Job Responsibilities 3.1 LTSA Commercial & Clause Control Participate in the pre-bidding and commercial docking of utility-scale energy storage projects, lead the negotiation, customization and review of LTSA long-term service agreements. Accurately control core terms including service scope, service term, performance assessment indicators (availability rate, MTBF, MTTR), liability for breach of contract, spare parts guarantee and price adjustment mechanisms. Establish standardized LTSA contract and risk ledgers, clarify service scope boundaries, avoid performance risks, unify the company’s LTSA service standards and commercial caliber, and provide professional service plan support and technical & commercial consultation for the sales team. 3.2 Full-Cycle Project Performance & O&M Management Take full responsibility for the performance of new and existing LTSA projects, and oversee the full lifecycle operation and maintenance services after grid connection, including daily inspection, regular maintenance, equipment troubleshooting and emergency repair, PCS/EMS/BMS system debugging and optimization, battery cluster performance calibration, and thermal management system operation. Strictly implement contractual service standards, track core KPIs such as power station availability, system performance and fault repair timeliness, regularly deliver project performance reports and performance analysis reports, and ensure 100% compliant project performance to meet owner and grid assessment requirements. 3.3 On-Site Resource & Spare Parts System Management Build a localized service system for utility-scale BESS LTSA projects, manage and dispatch on-site engineers, outsourced service providers and third-party O&M teams nationwide, and standardize on-site operating procedures, safety specifications and service standards. Establish a complete mechanism for spare parts warehousing, allocation, replacement and inventory checking. Accurately predict spare parts demand, control spare parts costs and logistics efficiency, solve on-site problems such as parts shortage, replacement and rework, ensure stable operation of power stations, and effectively reduce downtime and operation losses. 3.4 Fault Disposal & Technical Optimization Lead the disposal of major and complex faults of energy storage projects, identify root causes, formulate rectification plans, preventive mechanisms and optimization strategies, and summarize standardized solutions through case review. Based on power station operating data, battery attenuation rules and system operating problems, collaborate with R&D, engineering and quality teams to promote product iteration, program upgrade, structural optimization and O&M process improvement, so as to continuously enhance the stability, safety and service life of energy storage power stations and optimize long-term project operation quality. 3.5 Customer Relationship & Satisfaction Management Act as the core customer contact for LTSA projects, responsible for daily communication, monthly/quarterly O&M reports and project review docking.
